The wealth whose going makes one sit and grieve — in that wealth the minds of fools are fixed.
CD37: Virli = by the rare few. Sanchia = gathered. Piar = through love.
Rare people have lovingly gathered the true wealth of (Gopal's) pure Name.
How rare are those who gather the wealth of Truth, and love the Immaculate Naam, the Name of the Lord.
A few amass the wealth of truth and love the Immaculate Name.
Staying free of that, the pure and true wealth of Parmesar's Name has been gathered with love by (virli) a few people — that is, they have held it in the heart.
F9VK: Rachahi = you stay absorbed. Rang ek = in the love of the one Gopal.
(O Pandit! When the mind is joined to Gopal,) if wealth is lost, let it be lost,
If by losing your wealth, you may become absorbed in the Love of the One Lord, then just let it go.
If by losing wealth, you can be absorbed in the love of the One Lord, let it go then.
If the mind is absorbed in the love of the One and the wealth has gone, let it go.
ULRP: (but yes,) if you can be joined in the love of the one Prabhu, (for its sake) one should give even the mind and offer even the head; (having given all this) one should still rest one's hope on the (grace of the) Creator.
Dedicate your mind, and surrender your head; seek only the Support of the Creator Lord.
Deliver you your soul and also surrender your head to your Lord and seek you only your Creator's support.
Giving the mind, surrender also (sir) the sense of 'I'; and still take the (tek) refuge of the Creator alone — meaning, do not take pride in one's renunciation.
S0BQ: Those people in whose mind the (Satguru's) Shabad (comes to dwell), (in whom) the bliss (of Ram Nam comes) — they stop wandering in the affairs (of Maya),
Worldly affairs and wanderings cease, when the mind is filled with the bliss of the Shabad.
The worldly affairs and wanderings come to an end, when the Name's bliss enters into the man's mind.
When the bliss of the Shabad came into the mind and they met the (gur) worshipful Parmesar, then they ceased running after the affairs that there were.
VD8P: (because) on meeting the Guru, Parmatma, they turn from bad into good.
Even one's enemies become friends, meeting with the Guru, the Lord of the Universe.
Meeting with the Guru-God. even the enemies become friends.
When they met the (gur) worshipful Parmesar, those who were wicked became good people.
6CZ6: Basat = the (real) thing that is the 'Name'. Ghar = in the house. Bar = within the door.
(The soul-bride who, for the sake of that Prabhu's Name,) wandered searching forest after forest (did not find it, because) that (Name-)thing was in the heart, inside the house itself.
Wandering from forest to forest searching, you will find that those things are within the home of your own heart.
The things you wanderest for, searching forest to forest, abides within your very home.
Before, the intellect wandered (dhudhti) searching from forest to forest, while the treasure of the self remained (bar) within the (ghar) inner self.
KN8D: When the Satguru united her (with the Prabhu), she became joined (in His Name), and her suffering of birth and death came to an end. ||36||
United by the True Guru, you shall remain united, and the pains of birth and death will be ended. ||36||
United by the True Guru, you shall remain blended with the Lord and your pain of birth and death shall end.
Those whose intellect the Satgurus have joined — theirs stays joined. What was the fruit? The suffering of birth and death that there was has been (nivar) removed. ||36||
Y6VG: Nana = many deeds. Jam pur = into the city of Yama. Jahi = go.
By doing many (religious) deeds there can be no release (from pride); without singing Gopal's virtues, one falls into hell (because of this pride).
Through various rituals, one does not find release. Without virtue, one is sent to the City of Death.
Performing various rituals, one is released not. Without virtue, he goes to the city of death.
By doing many kinds of deeds one is not released from birth and death. Without the virtue of gyan one goes only to the city of Yama.
01V9: Tis = to that person. Ehu = this world. Ohu = the next world.

(The person who takes the support of mere 'deeds') gains neither this world nor the next (meaning, he has adorned neither the 'world' nor 'faith'); such people, staying caught in the fault (of ritualism), only repent in the end.
One will not have this world or the next; committing sinful mistakes, one comes to regret and repent in the end.
Committing sins, one grieves in the end and loses this world as also the yonder one,
Holding to (the wrong) qualities, the soul (phir) again repents. Neither is this world adorned for that soul, nor the next; or, neither did he gain this Maya, nor did he meet that Parmeshvar.

F8UN: Such a person gains neither a deep bond with Gopal, nor lofty attention, nor even dharma.
He has neither spiritual wisdom or meditation; neither Dharmic faith mor meditation.
He possesses neither gnosis nor concentration, neither faith nor meditation.
Neither did he attain gyan, nor was his meditation fixed on Bhagvan, nor was his attention fixed even on the deeds of dharma.
VHHN: Kaha = where? (meaning) is not found. Kia jana = cannot be understood.

(Because of this pride,) without the 'Name' the Fearless Prabhu cannot be attained; 'pride' cannot be understood (meaning, while staying in pride one does not even understand that the saddle of pride is on our back).
Without the Name, how can one be fearless? How can he understand egotistical pride?
Without the Name, how can he be fearless and how can he know the evil of ego?
How will this soul attain fearlessness without repeating the Name? And who knows what will become of this soul in the next world because of its pride? ☬ He shows the seeker's view:
ZLQH: Hath = the depth (of pride), the bottom.
(It is such an ocean that) its depth and far shore cannot be found; I have grown tired of trying, but could not find its end;
I am so tired - how can I get there? This ocean has no bottom or end.
I am tired. How can I get at my Lord, who is Unfathomable and Endless?
Doing many deeds, the intellect has grown tired. So how shall I reach Parmesar? The world-ocean has no bottom, and my own form, which is the far shore, is not in sight.
BVU4: Rangule = dyed, dyed in the Prabhu's love.
Apart from the gurmukhs dyed in Gopal's Name, this pain cannot even be told to anyone else.
I have no loving companions, whom I can ask for help.
I have not the loved friends, to whom I may cry for help.
The saints who are lovers have not come to me; so to whom shall I cry out?
JEKT: Priu = the Beloved. Kari = I do. Melanhar = the one able to unite.
O Nanak! If I remember that Beloved Prabhu again and again, then that Beloved, able to unite, Himself unites.
O Nanak, crying out, "Beloved, Beloved", we are united with the Uniter.
Nanak, if I utter the Name of my Beloved Groom, God, the Uniter, shall unite me with Himself.
Sri Guru ji says: if we say Husband, Husband, then (melanhar) Parmesar will unite us.
SB11: Jin = the (Prabhu) who. Het = through affection. Apar het = through boundless love. ||37||
The Prabhu who has separated (the soul, by placing the gap of 'pride') will unite it through the Guru's boundless love. ||37||
He who separated me, unites me again; my love for the Guru is infinite. ||37||
He, who separated me, will unite me with Himself, if I love the Guru infinitely.
The one who has separated this soul-bride because of her sins — that very Separator, with a glance of grace, will unite her by giving (het) boundless love for the Guru. ||37||
DG9A: (O Pandit!) Sin is a bad (deed), but it seems dear to the sinner,
Sin is bad, but it is dear to the sinner.
Sin is evil, but it is sweet to the sinner.
Sin is bad, yet it seems dear to the sinner.
65NZ: Pap = with sin. Pape = of sin alone. Pape pasara = only the spread of sin.
laden with sin, he spreads out only a spread of sin.
He loads himself with sin, and expands his world through sin.
He loads sins and through sin he makes ostentation.
He loads up sin — meaning, gathers it — and further causes others too to spread sins.
AAGE: Parhar = having given up. Aap = oneself.
If a person gives up sin and recognises his true self,
Sin is far away from one who understands himself.
He who sheds evil and understands his-self,
If, giving up sins, he recognises his own self —
JT5N: then worry, separation and suffering do not grip him.
He is not afflicted by sorrow or separation.
to him no sorrow, separation and suffering overtake.
he has neither the grief of separation, nor does suffering come to his body.
DFPG: Narak = in hell. Banchai = cheats, avoids.
(Otherwise) how can he escape falling into hell? And how can he avoid Yama (meaning, the fear of death)?
How can one avoid falling into hell? How can he cheat the Messenger of Death?
How can one escape falling into the hell? How can he save himself from death's courier?
How can this soul escape falling into hell, and how can it be saved from Yama, the Destroyer?
BUHV: Bura = bad. Jhuth bura = wretched falsehood. Jhuth bura kal = the bad death that is sin. Khai = destroys (spiritual life).
(So long as) falsehood, the death that is sin, is ruining (the soul's spiritual life), how can its birth and death end?
How can coming and going be forgotten? Falsehood is bad, and death is cruel.
How can one be rid of coming and going? Pernicious is falsehood and annihilating the death.
How shall its coming and going (visrai) cease — that is, stop? This soul embraces falsehood, which is bad; because of this, its (kal) Yama (khai) destroys it.
SUES: (So long as) the mind is surrounded by entanglements (of sin), it falls into further entanglements (of these sins),
The mind is enveloped by entanglements, and into entanglements it falls.
Man is enveloped with entanglements and in entanglements he ever falls.
This (man) soul is caught, wrapped in entanglement, and still keeps falling into entanglements.
NHHJ: Pachahi = burn. Pachahi pachahi = burn again and again. ||38||
Without Gopal's Name one cannot be saved (from these entanglements); (rather, beings) suffer again and again in their sins. ||38||
Without the Name, how can anyone be saved? They rot away in sin. ||38||
Without the Name, how can he be saved? In sin, he rots and putrefies.
Without the Name, how shall we be released? He himself rots in sins and makes his companions rot too. ||38||
P3C0: Kaua = a fool, a person of dark deeds.
The person of dark deeds is caught in the noose again and again,
Again and again, the crow falls into the trap.
Again and again, the crow falls into the net.
This soul, as a crow, again and again is caught in Yama's noose; then comes Yama's punishment.
Y5YS: (and once caught) he then repents: what has happened to me?
Then he regrets it, but what can he do now?
Then he grieves, but what can he do then?
Then he repents. Then the messengers of Yama say: what can be done now?
JZK1: Even though caught, it keeps pecking at the (very) feed (that caught it in the noose), and does not come to its senses.
Even though he is trapped, he pecks at the food; he does not understand.
Even when entrapped, he pecks at the food and understands not.
It is so caught in the world that, pecking at the feed of the sense-objects, it does not understand at all.
APFN: If the Satguru meets (it), then (the real thing) is seen with the eyes.
If he meets the True Guru, then he sees with his eyes.
If he meets the True Guru. then alone he sees with his eyes.
If it meets the Satgurus, then understanding comes to the eyes of the intellect.
F092: Jam jal = in the net of death, in the net that brings death.
Just as a fish is caught in the net that brings death (so the soul is caught in the sins that bring spiritual death).
Like a fish, he is caught in the noose of death.
Like a fish, the mortal is caught in the death's noose.
It is caught in Yama's net just as a fish is caught.
WM0X: (O Pandit!) Without the Guru, who gives (the gift of Gopal's Name), do not look for release (from this noose) (meaning, it is not found).
Do not seek liberation from anyone else, except the Guru, the Great Giver.
Without the Beneficent Guru, search not you salvation anywhere else.
Without the Gurus, the givers, do not seek liberation — that is, liberation is not attained.
9S8V: (The soul caught in this noose) is born and dies again and again.
Over and over again, he comes; over and over again, he goes.
Again and over again he comes and again and over again he goes.
Because of this it comes into the world again and again and goes again and again — that is, it is born and dies.
UKJV: Ik rang = in the love of the one Gopal.
The soul that joins itself in the love of the one Gopal and keeps its attention fixed
Be absorbed in love for the One Lord, and remain lovingly focused on Him.
If he is absorbed in the One Lord's love, he keeps his attention fixed in Him.
Those who are absorbed in the love of the One keep their awareness fixed.
HJPZ: in this way gets out of the noose of vices, and then no noose falls on it. ||39||
In this way you shall be saved, and you shall not fall into the trap again. ||39||
Thus is he emancipated and falls not in the trap again.
Those who are released (iv) in this way do not fall into Yama's noose again. ||39||
SRNA: Bira = O brother! Bairai = strangers, outsiders.
(O Pandit!) This body keeps saying 'brother, brother' (to the soul), (but when death comes) the brothers become strangers,
She calls out, "Brother, O brother - stay, O brother!" But he becomes a stranger.
She calls out, "OI brother, stay, O brother". But the brother becomes a stranger.
O brother! The intellect kept saying bira bira — that is, kept naming things again and again, meaning it kept wanting them. Those very things, at the appointed time, became enemies.
4948: Bahin = the sister, this body. Birah = in separation.
the brothers go (to the next world), to their own home, and the sister (the body) burns in separation (meaning, when death comes).
Her brother departs for his own home, and his sister burns with the pain of separation.
The brother leaves for his home and the sister burns herself stung by the pain of separation.
When the things went to their own home — that is, when they went to other men of merit — then the (bahin) sister, which is the intellect of things, burns in separation from them.
SEUS: Babul = the father. Kai ghar = in the house of. Babul kai ghar = in the parents' house, in this world. Betri = a little daughter. Bali balai neh = in the love of dolls and toys. Neh = in love.

(Even so, this) innocent little girl (the body), living in her father's house, stays absorbed in the love of dolls and toys (meaning, even knowing that the union of body and soul lasts only a few days, the soul stays absorbed in the things of the world).
In this world, her father's home, the daughter, the innocent soul bride, loves her Young Husband Lord.
While in this world or in her father's home, the daughter, deeming herself the young bride of her young Groom, should embrace love for Him.
(Babul) the father is ignorance; its (ghar) house is the world, and in it the soul is the daughter. This girl has love for (balai) things.
T6R6: (The soul should be taught this:) O (soul-)bride! If you want to meet the Husband (-Prabhu), then lovingly walk the path the Satguru has shown.
If you long for your Husband Lord, O soul bride, then serve the True Guru with love.
O bride, if you longer for your True Guru with love.
If the soul-bride desires (var) Parmeshvar, then let her serve the Satgurus (tehi) with love.
7JQ7: Bujhanau = one with understanding. Sach = through the true Prabhu, by Gopal's grace. Giani = the one of gyan, who has formed a deep bond with Parmatma.
The soul who meets the Satguru by Gopal's grace understands (this). But only some rare person gains this understanding.
How rare are the spiritually wise, who meet the True Guru, and truly understand.
Rare is the gnostic, who understands this by meeting with the True Satguru.
Only some rare gyani is (bujhanau) one with understanding; those who hold to it are few. Who is he? The one whom the true Satguru has met.
65JG: Singing the virtues of Gopal-Prabhu is in Gopal's own hands; (He gives this gift) to the one who pleases Him.
All glorious greatness rests in the Lord and Master's Hands. He grants them, when He is pleased.
The glories are in the hand of the Lord. Him alone He blesses with them whom He likes.
But these greatnesses are in the hands of the (thakur) Vahiguru; He gives them to whomever He wishes.
6F23: Some rare gurmukh reflects on the Satguru's bani;
How rare are those who contemplate the Word of the Guru's Bani; they become Gurmukh.
Some rare one, if he becomes resigned to Guru's will, reflects over the Guru's word.
Only some rare one reflects on the (bani) Guru's teaching. Whoever reflects on it is a gurmukh.
HEE2: Maha purakh = the Satguru. Nij ghar = in one's own home. ||40||
this bani of the Satguru is (such) that (by reflecting on it) a person becomes settled in his own true self. ||40||
This is the Bani of the Supreme Being; through it, one dwells within the home of his inner being. ||40||
This Gurbani is of the supreme person and through it, man abides in his own home.

This is the bani of the Great Being — that is, whoever holds the Guru's bani comes to dwell (nij ghar) in his own true form. Or: this bani, which is of the form of Oankar, sets forth the Great Being, Parmatma; by reflecting on its teaching one comes to dwell in one's own true form. ||40||
9A32: Bhan bhan = breaking again and again. Ghar ghar = shaping again and again. Usre = those built.
(This make-up of the world) is broken and shaped again and again, shaped and broken again and again.
Shattering and breaking apart, He creates and re-creates; creating, He shatters again. He builds up what He has demolished, and demolishes what He has built.
Breaking and crushing, the Lord fashions and while fashioning and making He again shatters. The demolished ones He builds and the built ones He demolishes.
Having broken, He shapes; the shape that has been made is (bhajai) destroyed by His own command. He builds up the fallen and tears down the built.
PZC6: Sokhai = dries up. Pokhai = fills to the brim.
(That Gopal) fills (this world-)pool and dries it up, then fills it to the brim again. That Gopal-Prabhu is able to do everything, and is carefree.
He dries up the pools which are full, and fills the dried tanks again. He is all-powerful and independent.
The Omnipotent, carefree Lord dries the filled-up tanks and again fully fills them.
The ponds that are full He dries up; again, those that are full He (pokhai) swells — that is, fills to overflowing.
8SPC: Bharam = in doubt. Kia paie = nothing is found.

(O Pandit! Forgetting that Gopal-Prabhu,) the beings who have fallen into wandering and gone astray are gone mad (after Maya); without good fortune they find nothing (in the way of the praise of that Carefree One).
Deluded by doubt, they have gone insane; without destiny, what do they obtain?
Strayed by doubt, men have become crazy, What can they obtain without destiny?
Led astray by doubt, these souls have become (divane) mad. Without good fortune, what reflection can they attain? That is, they cannot attain it.
Q29Y: Prabh = the Prabhu. Jin = those whom. Jaie = goes, is taken.

The Prabhu holds in (His own) hand the string of the Satguru's gyan; those whom He draws (towards Himself with this string) set out (towards Him) (meaning, those on whom Gopal-Prabhu shows grace walk the path the Guru has shown and are joined to His feet).
The Gurmukhs know that God holds the string; wherever He pulls it, they must go.
The Guru-ward knows, that the Lord holds the string, Whither the Lord draws, thither the mortals go.

The gurmukhs have themselves come to know that Parmesur holds the string of destiny — that is, Parmeshvar is the giver of the fruit of all beings' deeds. In whatever direction He pulls, in that direction one goes.
8N25: Singing the Prabhu's virtues, they stay absorbed in His love; they do not have to repent again.
Those who sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord, are forever imbued with His Love; they never again feel regret.
They, who sing God's praise and ever remain imbued with His love repent not in the end.
Those who, singing Hari's virtues, are ever dyed in love do not repent again.
F7X7: They search (for the Prabhu alone). (When) through the Satguru they understand (the way), then they settle in their own (true) home (and stop wandering).
Bhabha: If someone seeks, and then becomes Gurmukh, then he comes to dwell in the home of his own heart.
Bh: If they search and realise the Lord through the Guru, then your attain an abode in their own home.
Through bhabha he says: those who (bhalahi) search for the Satgurus, those gurmukhs understand. Those who understand come to dwell (nij ghar) in their own true form.
SHS5: Aas nirasa = becoming free of hopes.
This world-ocean is a hard road (for beings); it can be crossed only if we give up making (worldly) hopes,
Bhabha: The way of the terrifying world-ocean is treacherous. Remain free of hope, in the midst of hope, and you shall cross over.
Bh: Arduous is the way of the dreadful world-ocean. Remaining desireless among worldly desires, the world-ocean is crossed.
Through bhabha he says: the road of the world-ocean is very hard. If one becomes free of hope, then the crossing happens.
YXJ1: Aapo = oneself. Iv = in this way. ||41||
(and) by the Satguru's grace recognise our own self (our true being); in this way one dies while living (meaning, in this very life the mind turns away from vices). ||41||
By Guru's Grace, one comes to understand himself; in this way, he remains dead while yet alive. ||41||
By Guru's grace, the mortal understands his ownself and thus remains he dead in life.
And if, by the Guru's grace, one dies to the sense of separate self, then (iv) in this way one recognises one's own self; then the crossing happens. ||41||
52ET: (Countless beings) died pleading for Maya, but Maya stayed with no one,
Crying out for the wealth and riches of Maya, they die; but Maya does not go along with them.
Many have died crying for wealth and property, but wealth goes along with none.
Crying Maya, Maya, all have died; but Maya went with no one.
FZND: Dumano = double-minded (meaning, on one side caught here in Maya, on the other side death dragging it away by force). {Note: Farid ji writes in Raag Suhi "hans chalsi dumana". Compare Guru Nanak Dev ji's line "hans chalai uth dumano" with Farid ji's line. This sharing of words did not happen by chance; Guru Nanak Sahib had Farid ji's bani with him.} Aath = is. Bhuli aath = is forgotten, the companionship is broken.
When the (soul-)swan rises and departs, double-minded (when death comes), then its companionship with Maya is broken.
The soul-swan arises and departs, sad and depressed, leaving its wealth behind.
The soul-swan arises and departs crest-fallen and the wealth is forsaken over here.
The swan, the soul, rises and departs, and Maya is forgotten — meaning, Maya is left lying there.
GHS5: Jhutha = caught in false things, caught in Maya, which does not go along. Jam = Yama. Johia = eyed, threatened, frightened.
The mind caught in Maya is threatened by Yama (meaning, it is afraid at the very mention of death); (Maya stays here, and) the faults (committed for the sake of Maya) go along with it.
The false mind is hunted by the Messenger of Death; it carries its faults along when it goes.
The false soul is harassed by the Death's courier and one's demerits go along with him.
The (man) soul, which is false, has been (johia) looked upon by Yama; its faults go along with it.
ZRHU: Ulto = turning back from Maya, returning. Marai = dies to the sense of self.
But if a person has virtues in his lap, the mind turns back from Maya and dies to the sense of self within itself (meaning, attachment and the other vices do not remain in it).
The mind turns inward, and merges with mind, when it is with virtue.
If one be with virtues, his mind, turning its back upon the world, merges in the mind itself.
If good virtues go with the soul, then the mind's thoughts turn back and die within the mind itself.

AHAA: Forgetting Parmatma's 'Name', taking (mere) Maya to be their own, (countless beings) departed having only bought suffering (in this way);
Crying out, "Mine, mine!", they have died, but without the Name, they find only pain.
Puffed up with pride, many have perished. Without the Name, one comes to grief.
They have died crying mine, mine; without the Name, suffering will (bhal) come to them.
NQNG: Kaha = where did they go? They left one's side. Baji = a juggler's show. Dibanu = a court, rule. Garh = forts.
Forts, solid houses, palaces and mansions, and rule — (all) left one's side; they were only (a juggler's) show.
So where are their forts, mansions, palaces and courts? They are like a short story.
Where are the fortresses, mansions, palaces and courts? They are like the short-lived play.
What are (garh) forts, temples and solid palaces, and (diban) courts or halls of audience? All these are like the show of a conjuror — meaning, all are mere display, false.
R9J4: Jhutha = in vain. Aavan jan = coming and going, (meaning) the whole of life.
O Nanak! Without the Prabhu's Name the whole of life goes to waste;
O Nanak, without the True Name, the false just come and go.
Nanak, without the True Name, the false man continues coming and going.
Sri Guru ji says: without the true Name this soul is false; for it there remains only coming and going.
R4QV: (But what power does the poor soul have? It is without understanding.) The Prabhu Himself is wise, Himself knows everything (only if He makes it understand does the soul understand). ||42||
He Himself is clever and so very beautiful; He Himself is wise and all-knowing. ||42||
The Lord Himself is wise and beauteous and Himself accomplished and Omniscient.
He Himself, that (chatur) Parmeshvar, has become the form of all; He Himself is (sujan) clever to know their deeds. ||42||
9CDQ: Phun = again, in the same state, bound in attachment.
The beings who come (into the world bound in attachment to Maya) go (from here caught in this attachment), are born and die again, and suffer;
Those who come, must go in the end; they come and go, regretting and repenting.
They who come, shall ultimately go. Coming and going, they shall continue repenting.
Those who (aavahi) are born then (jahi) die; (aai gae) in coming and going they only repent.
1N5F: (for them) this creation of eighty-four lakh species does not lessen or grow in the least (meaning, because of attachment they have to pass through the eighty-four lakh species).
They will pass through 8.4 millions species; this number does not decrease or rise.
They shall pass through eighty-four lakhs of existences. This number decreases not, nor soars it high.

The eighty-four lakh births made on the (medni) earth and creation neither decrease nor increase upward — meaning, the full eighty-four lakh remain. Or: they do not decrease but increase — meaning, the soul does not come towards Parmesar, and day by day goes to a lower state.
NR0P: (Of them) only those are saved to whom the Prabhu seems dear,
They alone are saved, who love the Lord.
Only those persons are saved who love their Lord.
Those people are saved to whom the worship of Hari has been pleasing.
BQ1V: Viguti = was ruined. Viguti maia = Maya is ruined, Maya does not succeed in enticing them.
(because their) wandering (after Maya) comes to an end; Maya (coming towards them) is ruined (it cannot entice them).
Their worldly entanglements are ended, and Maya is conquered.
Their strife is ended and their desire for worldly valuable is dispelled.
Their worldly affairs have died away, and Maya, which was the deceiver, has been ruined. That is, knowing Maya to be false, they do not spread out their affairs.
NNPX: (In the world) whatever is seen is perishable; whom shall I make my friend?
Whoever is seen, shall depart; who should I make my friend?
Whosoever is seen, he shall go. Whom should I befriend then?
And this conviction has come to them: whatever comes into sight is bound to depart, in all three times. Whom shall we make our friend?
V71B: Sampau = I offer. Aagai deu = I place before as an offering.
(The friend who keeps company to the end is Parmatma alone; before Him) I offer my soul and place body and mind as an offering.
I dedicate my soul, and place my body and mind in offering before Him.
I surrender my mind to the Lord and my body and soul, I lay before Him.
To such a great soul I surrender my soul, and my body and mind, which have come to believe, I also give before him.
X8GP: O Creator! You alone are the ever-lasting Master. (O Pandit!) I have the support of the Creator alone.

then that being whose mind, out of this visible world, comes to be convinced by the Satguru's shabad obtains the highest spiritual state (then understand that) through the Guru's shabad the true Lord has absorbed (him into himself).

By pleasing the True Guru, the mortal attains the supreme status and merges in the True Name.

UN5N: (Then) he knows the one Lord alone (as the being that abides for ever); he has removed egotism and the sense of duality (that is, the thought of the possibility of any other such being apart from the Lord),

He alone is a Yogi, who understands the Guru's instruction and whose heart-lotus has bloomed.
